newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices ease on cool weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices ease on cool weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices turned softer Thursday due to cooler-than-normal forecasts throughout most of the U.S. this week, but steady storage buying prevented prices from cratering, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices fell two cents to the low-to-mid teens per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $2.16-2.19 and Transco (Station 65) pegged around $2.16-2.17.

Contributing to the downward trend, traders said, was the softer open on NYMEX, where July Henry Hub gas futures slipped to a low of $2.105, down 5.2 cents. By 1404 EDT, however, July recovered to $2.16.
As the cooler air moved toward the Southwest, Permian prices slumped by six cents to about $1.93-1.96, while Waha values were quoted in the low-$2 area.

Southern California prices, however, climbed three cents to about $2.15 as temperature highs were forecast to move into the low-80s Friday and Saturday in Los Angeles, according to Weather Services Corp.
In the Midwest, where mild weather is also keeping buyers on the sidelines, prices slipped two cents to about $2.00-2.02.
Chicago city-gate prices were also quoted lower at $2.20, with temperatures forecast to reach highs in the mid-to-high 60s over the next two days.

New York city gate prices also eased by a few cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s as temperatures were expected to hover about five to 10 degrees below normal in the Northeast through early next week, according to WSC.
Appalachian values drifted about one cent lower to the low-$2.30s, traders said.

Separately, American Gas Association said Wednesday that gas stocks in the U.S. last week were up 93 bcf to 38 percent of capacity. In the East, stocks rose 62 bcf to 32 percent full, while western stocks remained 41 bcf behind year-ago levels at 229 bcf.
